MoCA 19/30 with losses in trail-making, cube, clock, digit span backwards, serial sevens, fluency (8 animals) and delayed recall (2/5 unaided, 4/5 cued). patient.chief_complaint: Cognitive decline since aortic valve replacement five months ago that has not improved with recovery
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Roberto Vanni is a 68-year-old retired engineer who underwent surgical aortic valve replacement five months ago. The operation was complicated by prolonged intraoperative hypotension and 36 hours of vasopressor support; he was slow to wake and had a period of postoperative confusion which was documented as delirium and treated as such. His wife reports that the confusion resolved within two weeks but that he never returned to his baseline. Five months on, he cannot manage the household administration he ran until the surgery, cannot follow a two-step instruction, loses the thread of a task, and has abandoned the model engineering he did for forty years because he cannot plan the sequence of steps. His memory for events is reasonable and improves with prompting. Physically he has recovered well and walks a kilometre. There has been no fluctuation in alertness, no hallucination, no dream enactment and no further abrupt event. His blood pressure is now well controlled at 128/72, and his renal function deteriorated perioperatively and has partly recovered.

additional_observations: The infarcts are symmetric and confined to arterial border zones — cortical watersheds and the internal border zone of the centrum semiovale bilaterally
A symmetric bilateral border-zone distribution is the signature of global hypoperfusion, not of embolism, which scatters asymmetrically
No restricted diffusion; the lesions date to the perioperative period
Minimal small-vessel burden at Fazekas 1 and normal hippocampi — neither small-vessel disease nor a degenerative process contributes materially
mri.impression: Symmetric bilateral cortical and internal border-zone infarction with a minimal small-vessel burden and normal medial temporal lobes. The distribution is that of global hypoperfusion and corresponds to the documented prolonged intraoperative and postoperative hypotension.

findings: Sinus rhythm at 64 bpm with first-degree AV block

ecg.interpretation: Sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block and left ventricular hypertrophy from the treated valve disease. No atrial fibrillation here or on postoperative telemetry, which argues against a cardioembolic mechanism and leaves the documented hypotensive episode as the explanation for a border-zone pattern.

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia due to global hypoperfusion — bilateral cortical and internal border-zone infarction sustained during prolonged perioperative hypotension at aortic valve replacement

differential.diagnosis: Persistent postoperative cognitive dysfunction without structural injury
differential.key_features: A recognised entity after cardiac surgery and the default assumption in this scenario, but here there is structural injury on MRI in a distribution that explains the deficit, which changes it from a functional diagnosis to a demonstrated one
The 4AT is 0, alertness has been stable for months and there is no fluctuation; the delirium resolved and the deficit did not

differential.diagnosis: Cardioembolic infarction from the surgery or the prosthesis
differential.key_features: Embolic showers do occur with valve surgery, but the distribution here is symmetric and confined to border zones, the echocardiogram shows no thrombus or vegetation, and no arrhythmia has been documented
Cue-responsive recall, normal hippocampi and a purely dysexecutive profile with no pre-surgical decline reported
Geriatric Depression Scale 5/15 with structural injury present and objective dysexecutive deficits

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Cognitive decline dating precisely to a cardiac operation complicated by prolonged hypotension, with a documented delirium that resolved but left a persistent dysexecutive deficit, and no subsequent progression

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 19/30 with a dysexecutive and attentional profile, cue-responsive recall, a negative delirium screen and informant-documented loss of instrumental independence

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; residual perioperative renal impairment and mild anaemia documented, with lipids near target

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Symmetric bilateral cortical and internal border-zone infarction with Fazekas 1 change and normal hippocampi — the signature of global hypoperfusion rather than embolism

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to look for atrial fibrillation as the embolic source and for the left ventricular hypertrophy of chronic hypertension
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block and left ventricular hypertrophy; no atrial fibrillation here or on postoperative telemetry, arguing against cardioembolism

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a transthoracic echocardiogram to look for a structural cardioembolic source
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Well-functioning prosthetic aortic valve with no thrombus or vegetation and preserved systolic function — no cardioembolic source, which leaves hypoperfusion as the mechanism

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Dysexecutive and attentional profile with preserved recognition memory, matching bilateral border-zone injury rather than a degenerative gradient

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Protect perfusion: avoid over-treatment of blood pressure and set an individualised target rather than driving the systolic below 120 mmHg in a patient with established border-zone injury, review the diuretic for volume depletion, maintain the statin and antiplatelet, refer for cognitive rehabilitation targeting executive function, and document the injury clearly for future anaesthetic planning
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Blood-pressure target individualised upward to protect border-zone perfusion, diuretic reviewed, cognitive rehabilitation arranged, and the perioperative injury documented for future surgical and anaesthetic planning

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Date the cognitive change against the operation and distinguish resolved delirium from a persistent deficit with a formal delirium screen
Document the deficit and its functional consequence with an informant-rated scale
Obtain brain MRI: a symmetric border-zone distribution identifies the mechanism and converts a presumed functional problem into a demonstrated injury
Exclude an embolic source with an ECG and echocardiography, because the treatment implications differ entirely
Individualise the blood-pressure target upward where border-zone injury is established, rather than applying a standard aggressive target
Record the injury and the hypotensive aetiology for future anaesthetic planning
contraindicated_actions: Do not dismiss persistent cognitive impairment after cardiac surgery as expected postoperative cognitive dysfunction without imaging
Do not drive the systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg in a patient with established border-zone infarction
Do not start anticoagulation: there is no embolic source and the mechanism is haemodynamic
Do not continue an unnecessary diuretic in a patient at risk from volume depletion and hypotension
Do not treat the residual deficit as delirium with antipsychotics
key_reasoning_points: Symmetry and location identify the mechanism: bilateral infarction confined to cortical watersheds and the internal border zone is haemodynamic, whereas emboli produce asymmetric lesions in vessel territories
Postoperative cognitive dysfunction is a diagnosis of exclusion, and imaging here shows a structural lesion that explains the deficit — which changes both the prognosis and the management
A resolved delirium and a persistent dysexecutive deficit are different things, and a formal screen separates them months later
Established border-zone injury inverts the usual blood-pressure advice: perfusion depends on pressure in territories with exhausted reserve, so the target is individualised upward
Documenting a hypotensive brain injury changes the conduct of any future anaesthetic, which makes recording it a therapeutic act

red_herrings.data_point: A documented episode of postoperative delirium
red_herrings.intended_effect: Explains the whole picture as postoperative cognitive dysfunction after delirium and stops the investigation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The delirium resolved in two weeks and the 4AT is now 0, while the dysexecutive deficit has persisted for five months and is explained by structural border-zone injury on MRI

red_herrings.data_point: Recent valve surgery, a recognised source of cerebral emboli
red_herrings.intended_effect: Prompts a search for a cardioembolic source and consideration of anticoagulation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The infarct distribution is symmetric and confined to border zones, which is haemodynamic; echocardiography shows no thrombus or vegetation and no arrhythmia has been recorded

key_educational_points: Symmetric bilateral border-zone infarction is the imaging signature of global hypoperfusion
Persistent cognitive impairment after cardiac surgery deserves imaging rather than a default label of postoperative cognitive dysfunction
Established border-zone injury changes the blood-pressure target upward
Recording a hypotensive brain injury alters future anaesthetic planning
